paper_title: Ethylene modulates cell wall mechanics for root responses to compaction
access: Full journal HTML including main results, figure captions, and methods read; original article open access CC BY 4.0. No reliance on an abstract alone.

verified_claims.claim: In compacted soil, cesa6 rice roots were longer than wild type, while lengths were similar in germination pouches.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Reduced cellulose aids root penetration; Figure 1a–d.

verified_claims.claim: Non-compacted and compacted soil treatments used bulk densities of 1.2 and 1.6 g cm−3. Main CT comparisons examined 5-day-old seedlings.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Methods: Soil compaction details; X-ray CT imaging; Figure 1 caption.

verified_claims.claim: OsARF1 binds regulatory regions of several CESA genes and represses promoter activity; dense conditions increase its expression particularly in the cortex.
verified_claims.evidence_location: OsARF1 binds CESA promoters; Figure 2b–f; Figure 3a–b.

verified_claims.claim: Compacted soil reduced wild-type root length by 35% and OE-ARF1 root length by 19% in the reported comparison.
verified_claims.evidence_location: OsARF1 controls root penetration via CESA; Figure 3f,h.

verified_claims.claim: Cortex wall thinning and expansion were associated with cellulose regulation; dense media produced thicker epidermal walls.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Roots modify cell walls under compaction; Figure 4a–g.

verified_claims.claim: The authors explicitly caution that AFM on sectioned material gives comparative values rather than in-vivo wall stiffness.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Roots modify cell walls under compaction, paragraph explaining AFM; Methods: Cell wall stiffness experimental details.

verified_claims.claim: Ethylene precursor treatment strongly induced OsARF1, and ethylene-pathway mutants were tested; the authors leave other hormonal relationships unresolved.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Compaction induces OsARF1 via ethylene; Figure 4h–j; Extended Data Figure 10.

limitations: Rice seedling experiments, not a sorghum trial or a multi-location yield trial.
Controlled agar and packed-soil conditions are not equivalent to heterogeneous fields.
Wall stiffness measured on prepared sections cannot be directly treated as intact-root stiffness.
Thin ethylene-insensitive roots can also penetrate well, so root width alone is not a general predictor.
Buckling and stability explanations are mechanistic interpretations rather than direct measurements of all forces in living roots.
application_status: Proposed sorghum measurements and coupled CPlantBox/DuMuX hypotheses are explicitly marked as extrapolation. No claim is made that these tools already implement the pathway or that rice parameters transfer to sorghum.
